passage: In rural India, the life of a farmer is dictated by the seasons. Unlike factory workers who have a steady schedule, a farmer only finds work during the sowing and harvesting months, leaving them without income for the rest of the year. To survive, many rural families migrate to cities to find daily wage work. In the city, the reality of employment is quite different. A street vendor, for instance, works long hours setting up stalls and managing stock, yet they often lack the security of a permanent job. Many people mistakenly believe that these vendors are simply lazy, but in truth, they are hardworking individuals who lack the capital to rent a formal shop. Furthermore, city jobs are not uniform. While some employees in large offices enjoy benefits like medical leave and pensions, many others work in informal sectors where such protections do not exist. Therefore, whether in a village or a city, livelihood depends heavily on the nature of the work rather than just the location. Understanding these differences helps us see why some people struggle to find stable income, regardless of how hard they try to earn a living.

items.evidence: Unlike factory workers who have a steady schedule, a farmer only finds work during the sowing and harvesting months, leaving them without income for the rest of the year.
items.q: It is a month between harvest and the next sowing. What is a farmer's situation then?
options: He has hardly any work and earns nothing
He works and earns the same as always
He works a steady schedule like factory workers
He gets a monthly salary from his employer
items.explain: Farmers find work only in sowing and harvesting months, so they have no income at other times.

wrong.why: thinks farm work and earnings are equal every month
thinks farmers have work all year
thinks self-employed farmers are paid a salary

items.evidence: To survive, many rural families migrate to cities to find daily wage work.
items.q: Why do many rural families leave their villages for cities?
options: To earn some money each day and survive
To get office jobs with pensions
To rent formal shops in the market
To get a fixed salary every month
items.explain: With no farm income for months, families move to cities to find daily wage work and survive.

wrong.why: thinks all city jobs give pensions
picks a nearby detail about vendors' shops
thinks daily wage work has a fixed monthly salary

items.evidence: Many people mistakenly believe that these vendors are simply lazy, but in truth, they are hardworking individuals who lack the capital to rent a formal shop.
items.q: A street vendor works very hard but still sells from the roadside. Which explains this?
options: He lacks the money to rent a proper shop
He is too lazy to manage a real shop
He needs no stock or effort on the road
He prefers the job security of a stall
items.explain: Vendors are hardworking but lack the capital to rent a formal shop, so they sell on the road.

wrong.why: thinks vendors are poor because they are lazy
thinks road selling needs no work or buying
reverses the passage, which says vendors lack security

items.evidence: While some employees in large offices enjoy benefits like medical leave and pensions, many others work in informal sectors where such protections do not exist.
items.q: Meena works in the city's informal sector and falls ill. What can she expect?
options: She gets no paid medical leave at all
She gets paid medical leave like every city worker
She gets leave only if her boss is government
She keeps getting a fixed salary while resting
items.explain: Informal sector jobs do not have protections like medical leave and pensions, unlike some large offices.

wrong.why: thinks all city jobs give medical leave
thinks formal benefits mean only government jobs
thinks informal workers have a fixed monthly salary
